trolley_hub: ^A runaway trolley is moving toward five workers on the main track. They cannot leave the track in time.
^Beside you is a lever that will divert the trolley onto a side track, where one worker is standing.
trolley_choice: ^The trolley cannot be stopped. Pulling the lever will redirect it; leaving the lever untouched will preserve its current course.

c-0: ^The mechanism is simple: one movement changes who is placed in danger.
^Pulling it would make the redirection deliberate. Leaving it untouched would allow the existing course to continue.
c-1: ^Five people are trapped on the main track. Each has the same immediate claim to survival as the person on the side track.
c-2: ^One person stands on the side track, currently outside the trolley's path.
^Diverting the trolley would place that person in danger in order to spare the five.
c-4: ^I will redirect it. One person will die, but five will otherwise die on the current track.
^You intervene and reduce the number of deaths, while making the single worker's death a consequence of your action.
c-5: ^I will not redirect the trolley. The five remain in danger, but I will not place the worker on the side track in its path.
^You preserve the existing course and avoid using one person as the means of saving the others, while allowing five preventable deaths.
c-6: ^Heads: pull the lever. Tails: leave it untouched.
^The procedure is impartial, but choosing the procedure is still a moral decision.

coin_result: ^(The coin turns in the air and lands against the metal housing.)
^Tails. According to the rule I chose, I should leave the lever untouched.
^The result does not compel you. It only returns the decision in a form you agreed to follow.

c-0: ^I chose the procedure before knowing the outcome. I will follow it, even though five people will die.
c-1: ^I used chance to avoid favouring either side, but I am not willing to accept this outcome. I will pull the lever.

end_dilemma: ^(The sound of wheels and metal returns all at once.)
